summary: Vrajavallabha Dvivedi worked in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy. He headed the Yogatantra Department at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University and served as Deputy Director at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1990-1992).
W. F. Jayasuriya worked in the field of Buddhist studies. He studied under H. D. Dharmasiriwardhana, M. U. Sri Kaveeswara, and Rerukane Ariyaratne (attested 1963).

W. H. D. Rouse worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cheltenham, Regent's Park, and Cambridge (Christ's College), he taught at Bedford, Cheltenham, and Rugby, and served as headmaster of The Perse School (1902-1928).

W. H. R. Rivers was a history, archaeology, and medical scholar. Trained in medicine at London and St Bartholomew's, he held various hospital posts, taught at Cambridge and London, and presided over the Anthropological Society of London (circa 1921-1922).

W. Norman Brown worked in Indology, history/archaeology, and linguistics. He studied at Hiram and Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield, later holding posts at Johns Hopkins, Government Sri Pratap Memorial Rajput College, and the University of Pennsylvania (circa 1926-1966).

W. Randolph Kloetzli, an Indology, Buddhist, and religious studies scholar, earned a PhD at the University of Chicago (1964), studying under mentors including Mircea Eliade and Paul Tillich. He lectured at American University, George Washington University, and Dartmouth College.

W. S. Karunatillake worked in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He served as Professor at the University of Kelaniya (attested 1997) and was Visiting Numata Professor of Buddhist Studies at Harvard University in 1998.

Wai-lun Tam works in religious studies, sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at McMaster University under Koichi Shinohara (attested 1996) and became a professor and department chairperson at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (attested 2016).

Walpola Rahula was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies scholar. Educated at Ceylon, Calcutta, and Paris (Sorbonne), he served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Sri Jayewardenepura (1964-1969) and professor at Northwestern University (1964).

Walter Bruno Henning worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. After studying at the University of Göttingen (circa 1926-1930), he held posts at SOAS/University of London (circa 1936-1961), Columbia, and UC Berkeley (circa 1961-1967).

Walter Elliot worked in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics. He studied at the East India Company College (circa 1818-1820) and the College of Fort St George, and served as Private Secretary to Lord Elphinstone in Madras (1837-1842).

Walter Eugene Clark, an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, earned his degrees at Harvard and studied under Richard Pischel. He taught Sanskrit at the University of Chicago (1923-1927) and Harvard University as Wales Professor (1927-1950).

Walter Liebenthal, a sinologist, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, completed his doctorate at Breslau (circa 1928-1933). He held posts at Peking University, Visva-Bharati University, the Sorbonne, and the University of Tübingen (1965-1982).

Walter M. Spink was an art historian and Indologist who earned his BA at Amherst and his PhD at Harvard (circa 1949-1954). He taught at Brandeis University (1956-1961) and served as Professor at the University of Michigan (circa 1961-2000).

Walter Nowick was a Buddhist studies scholar and teacher. He studied at the Juilliard School and under Zuigan Goto (1950-1965), founded Moonspring Hermitage, and held a post at Kyoto Women's University.

Walter Piston studied at the Massachusetts College of Art and Design (circa 1914-1920) and Harvard University (circa 1920-1924). He subsequently served on the faculty at Harvard University from circa 1926 to 1960.

Walter Porzig, an Indology and linguistics scholar, studied at the University of Jena (circa 1914-1920) under Wilhelm Streitberg. He held faculty posts at the universities of Leipzig, Bern, Jena, and Mainz (circa 1951-1961).
Walter Ruben was an Indologist. He held academic posts at Goethe University Frankfurt (circa 1931-1935), the University of Chile (circa 1948-1949), and the University of Berlin (circa 1950-1965).

Walter Simon specialized in sinology, Tibetology, and linguistics, studying at the University of Berlin. He held posts at the University of Berlin (1919-1937) and later served as Professor of Chinese at the University of London/SOAS (1947-1960).

Walter Slaje is an Indologist who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Graz University Library and later served as Director at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg (1995-2020).
